residents.name: Hesketh Fell and the last tree
residents.kind: a named Pokemon in plain sight, and the man who has not noticed: the joke is the meeting
residents.situation: In the birch woods of the Viltri plateau a woodcutter has cleared a round of ground thirty blocks across: sawdust and chips, a ring of fresh birch stumps, a woodpile, a chopping block and a grindstone. In the middle of the clearing stands the one thing he has not felled, which he takes for an oak in a birch wood and has been at for six weeks: three axes bounced off it and the third one bent. Hesketh Fell has the felling order for the whole wood and means to finish it. The 'oak' is Old Knot, a Sudowoodo, who stands very still in the middle of a clearing that used to be its forest and wakes only when somebody walks right up to it.
residents.story_rule: Hesketh never says Sudowoodo and never works it out; the dialogue lets the player tell him and he does not believe it. Sudowoodo dislikes water in the main series, which is the one thing he has noticed (it 'went and stood under the birches' when it rained). Tier 1, the first wood out of the first gym town, so the joke is one an early player can get

residents.name: Agnes Merrow's carving
residents.kind: something read for someone who cannot read it any more: the answer is out in the wood, on a tree, and the player has to go and look
residents.situation: In a clearing in the foothill woods stands a bow-top wagon, red sides, white canvas, its shafts resting on the ground and no horse in sight for years. Agnes Merrow has lived in it for sixty-one of them. The morning she married Edwin, he carved their initials into the old oak on the rise sixty paces north, and then went round the back of the tree and carved something else, and laughed, and never would tell her what. 'You'll read it when you need to,' he said. Edwin is gone and the oak is dead and Agnes cannot see past her own hand. She asks the player to go and read it to her. The front of the tree says what she knows; the back says what he never told her. She knows the front by heart, so a player who only reads the front is sent back round.
residents.story_rule: the carving is the only clue and it is on the tree: the dialogue offers three readings, only one of which is written there. A guess can land it (one in three, retried freely): the puzzle is honest, not secure, and says so in data/quests.json evt_agnes_carving answer_check. residents.kind: a character who grows with the player's badges: a different conversation at every visit from the fourth badge to the eighth, and a gift at the end
residents.situation: Out on the open downs past Greenhollow, a ten-year-old has built a gym. The battlefield is scratched into the turf with a stick: the lines, the halfway line, the circle. There is a podium of hay bales, a row of hay for the crowd, a 'Geodude (pretend)' made of hay, and a gate for challengers. Pip has no Pokemon (her mum says when she is eleven), but she has a sign that says PIP'S GYM, a badge called the Twig Badge that nobody has won, and a leader's speech that is nearly finished. She worships Erika. Every time the player comes back with another badge she wants to know everything about that leader, and when the player comes back with all eight she makes them the first winner of the Twig Badge.

residents.name: The Wandering Stone
residents.kind: a local mystery whose answer is a Pokemon: the place sets the question in five hands over five generations, and the answer is asleep behind the stone
residents.situation: On the dead-flat fields below the glacier lies one great boulder of a rock that is not from here, the way a glacier leaves one. Behind it, to the west, runs a furrow of torn earth forty blocks long, as if the stone had been dragged; in front of it, on the east, the turf is heaped up like a bow wave. Along the furrow stand five marker stones, each with a sign, each in a different hand, each saying the stone stood HERE: the oldest mossed over ('the year of the long frost'), a grandfather's ('the year the bridge went'), a child's ('grandad says it never moves - E.W. age 9'), the same family a generation later ('E.W. was right'), and the newest in capitals: 'LAST SPRING. WHO IS PUSHING IT.' In the furrow, with its shoulder to the stone, sleeps what looks like one more boulder. It is Heave, an old Golem, and every spring it pushes.
residents.story_rule: no NPC: the five signs are the whole story, and they never name the Golem. They are the people of the fields (the Wick family, by the initials) over about five generations; the glacier-foot fields have no town, and nothing here claims more about who they were. Tier 5, between Fenhide and Tilpey Cross

residents.name: Tam's home base
residents.kind: a search: someone is lost on purpose, and the player is asked to find them. Two records, one meeting: Tam here, his twin Lettie in hide_and_seek_den
residents.situation: In the open woods of the Tilpey east shore, a boy of nine stands with his face to a post marked HOME BASE, counting. Tam Furrow and his twin sister Lettie started a game of hide and seek this morning. He has counted to a hundred eleven times. She has not been found and will not come out until she is found properly, and their mum will be calling them in for tea. He asks the player to help. Lettie is seventy blocks away up the bank, inside a hollow in a spruce thicket, with biscuits and a blanket, in no hurry at all. When the player has found her and come back, Tam gives them two bottles of his mum's Moomoo Milk, one for each twin.
residents.story_rule: Tam's hints are true and not enough: 'somewhere low, or somewhere high', and 'I don't like under things' (she is under something). The finding is Lettie's conversation, which sets a field Tam's conversation reads (data/quests.json evt_hide_and_seek_den found). Tier 6, an afternoon's walk from Tilpey Cross; nothing here is about the tier but the reward's size

residents.name: Cassius Rook's high seat
residents.kind: a choice made for someone else: the player decides whether to tell a hunter where the thing he has waited for is, and he lives with the answer
residents.situation: In the birch woods above the Tilpey north shore stands a hunter's high seat: four spruce legs, a ladder, a railed platform with a roof, a camp fire below and a tally board. Cassius Rook has sat up there every dawn for eleven seasons for the Tilpey Hart, as his father did and his grandfather. He has seen it four times and never close. Eighty blocks down the slope to the south-east, in a hollow under the birches, is the bed it sleeps in: flattened ground and a birch it has rubbed its antlers bare on. The Hart is a Sawsbuck, very old, and wakes if anyone comes within ten blocks. Cassius asks the player whether they saw it on the way up. The player can tell him about the hollow, or say they saw nothing. Either way he thanks them, and either way he is still sitting there on every later visit.
residents.story_rule: nothing changes in the world on either answer: the Hart stays in its hollow, and Cassius keeps his seat ('first light, I said. Tomorrow's first light'). The choice is recorded only in his conversation. The dialogue cannot tell whether the player has seen the hollow; a player who has not and says so anyway is telling him something true by accident, which the quest records note. Tier 6, the north shore of Lake Tilpey
